title: Routing: enforce Dedicated staged rollout traffic weights with deterministic bucketing + 0/100% guardrails
author: Ravi Menon
description: Context: Dedicated pools are reserved and high-SLA; for staged rollouts we need deterministic, enforceable traffic allocation per stage without cross-tenant interference, and we need guardrails around 0%/100% transitions to avoid accidental full cutovers or “all traffic drops” due to rounding/config errors. What changed: This PR adds a routing-time stage allocator for Dedicated pools that computes a stable bucket (0..9999) from a non-PII key (tenant_id, pool_id, route_id, rollout_plan_id, rollout_plan_version, and an optional sticky token when provided) and maps that bucket to a stage based on cumulative weights. Allocation is deterministic across pods/processes and does not rely on local state. Guardrails: (1) If weights sum != 100, we clamp and emit a structured warning + metric and treat the remainder as baseline traffic; (2) Explicit fast-paths for total 0%/100% (skip hashing when candidate is 100%, and treat candidate=0% as “no-op” while preserving baseline route selection); (3) Disallow “all stages 0%” (hold to baseline + emit error) to prevent blackholing traffic; (4) When plan_version changes, we include plan_version in the hash key to avoid mixing allocations across versions during propagation; (5) Enforced tenant isolation by scoping bucketing to (tenant_id, pool_id) so Dedicated pools do not share buckets. Observability: Adds `routing_rollout_stage_selected_total{pool_id,stage_id}` (pool_id sampled/hashed to reduce cardinality), `routing_rollout_weight_sum_mismatch_total`, and debug logging behind `ROUTING_ROLLOUT_DEBUG=1` which prints the chosen bucket and stage for a request. Testing: Unit tests for determinism, boundary conditions (0/100, partial sums, multiple stages), and a regression test that verifies baseline fallback when plan is missing or evaluator marks the rollout as HOLD. Notes: This PR only applies stage weight selection in the router; gates/advancement state machine come from control plane/evaluator work and are consumed via the existing rollout policy snapshot. Follow-ups: add an admin-only header override to force a specific bucket for reproducibility in incident triage; evaluate a consistent-hash strategy for “minimal movement” when weights change (not required for v1 deterministic staged rollouts).
commits: routing: add dedicated rollout stage allocator (deterministic bucket mapping)
routing: guardrails for weight sum mismatch + 0/100% fast paths
routing: baseline fallback when rollout policy snapshot is HOLD/invalid
metrics: add stage selection counters + mismatch warning metric
tests: determinism + boundary cases for stage allocation
review_conversation: Mina Haddad (review): Determinism looks good. Two questions: (1) why include plan_version in the hash? (2) what happens if weights sum to 99 due to UI rounding?

Ravi Menon (author): (1) Plan version is included to prevent mixed allocations when a new plan is rolled out gradually across routers; otherwise two routers could disagree for the same request key. (2) We clamp + emit `routing_rollout_weight_sum_mismatch_total` and treat the remainder as baseline traffic; also added a structured warning with tenant_id + pool_id + plan_id so SRE can spot misconfigs.
Jordan Lee (review): Can we ensure the hash key doesn’t accidentally pull request_id or user identifiers? Also, I’m worried about “all stages 0%” config blackholing.

Ravi Menon (author): Hash input is strictly control-plane identifiers + optional sticky token (random, generated by our edge when enabled). No request_id/user_id included. Added a hard guard: if all configured stages have 0%, allocator returns BASELINE and increments an error counter.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): Tenant isolation: do we ever bucket across pools? Dedicated must not. Please add an explicit comment and a test that tenant_id+pool_id affect output.
Ravi Menon (author): Added a test case verifying same route_id/plan_id but different pool_id produces different bucket/stage; also added comments in `stage_allocator.ts` about Dedicated scoping.
Sean Gallagher (review): For 100% candidate, can we skip hashing for hot path? Also please confirm metrics cardinality is bounded; pool_id label scares me.

Ravi Menon (author): Added 100% fast-path (no hashing). For metrics, pool_id is emitted as `pool_hash` (stable hash prefix) by default; full pool_id label is behind `ROUTING_METRICS_HIGH_CARDINALITY=1` and only for staging/debug.
Elena Popov (review): Capacity-aware fallback: if candidate stage routes to a model variant that’s currently constrained, does this PR handle fallback to baseline?

Ravi Menon (author): Not directly; this PR only selects stage weights. The actual target selection still goes through the existing capacity-aware resolver which can fall back. Added a test ensuring that if resolver returns `NO_CAPACITY`, we retry baseline within the same pool.
Mina Haddad (approval): Approved after latest push. Please keep follow-up for bucket override header in a separate PR.
Sean Gallagher (approval): LGTM; thanks for the metrics cardinality guard.
release_notes: Internal: Dedicated routing now supports deterministic staged rollout traffic weights (stage bucket allocation), with safety guardrails for misconfigured 0%/100% and weight sums. Adds routing metrics for selected stage + mismatch warnings.
